changes: Guild history becomes an original 39-episode novel covering all 28 guild-board commission entries from F-rank through the finale. The 27 established chapter IDs remain; 12 new episodes make escorts, rescue, infestation, repeatable bounties, extraction and the splitting raid visible in the story. The prose expands from 5,235 to 14,636 words, plus 1,802 words of guide notes.

Each episode has an expandable Quest guide with objectives, progression gates and supported branches. Both ends retain Previous/Next navigation. The reader identifies this as one dramatized spoiler route; reading does not accept a quest, award an item or change player progression. No fixed 1,000-quest requirement is added.

The recruit has a practical original voice: useful loot, supply costs, awkward early victories and increasingly reliable field judgment. The 1,065-word Mastermind episode draws on the earlier jobs. No hack, fourth-wall exploit, borrowed novel passage, recreated outside scene or new identity reveal is introduced.

Mastermind combat uses fixed encounter-only STR 2d8+2, CON 3d8+2, INT 3d8+2 and AGI 2d10+2 in place of the weak generic avatar baseline. His existing two reserve calls, one Protect Orb and one Elixir remain finite. Fire and Defense remain repeatable. The ordinary avatar and other encounters retain their stats.

Protect Orb item wards are now recognized by tactical melee, projectiles, dash attacks and the ward display. Zero-charge wards no longer absorb extra hits while awaiting their owner’s next turn. Spell wards and item wards both stop exactly the remaining number of successful hits, for either side.
All 69 Fool/Dark Emperor entries, guild quest definitions, stronghold/finale progression and rewards, Solgata’s disappearance, the world terrain and the complete server are unchanged.

validation.method: Actual HTML startup in Node/jsdom with canvas/audio/socket stubs, native reader navigation across all 108 lore entries, actual tactical action and update paths, finite enemy inventory, encounter-only stat rolls, save preservation, and existing world/HUD regressions. No browser, phone rendering, live server or combat-balance playtest claim. Server code and packages are unchanged and syntax checked.

limitations: The revised boss’s balance, phone visuals, touch feel and performance require a real playthrough. Automated fixtures verify rules and state transitions, not subjective difficulty or literary satisfaction.

The novel dramatizes one route. Generated target locations and ordinary rewards vary; optional and random branches remain available. Dialogue and incidental action are prose rather than added cutscenes.
This release does not deploy the game or change the server, maps, class paths, Phoenix Empress storyline, attack animations or the Fool/Dark Emperor archive.
